newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIAN GOVT WORKS TO REBUILD FLOODED MINING TOWN.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIAN GOVT WORKS TO REBUILD FLOODED MINING TOWN.

text.p: The government said on Thursday it was battling to restore water and power supplies to the mining town of Maamba after heavy flooding in the area over the past few days.

Southern province permanent secretary Sylvester Mpishi said residents had been living without clean water, electricity and medical supplies for days after heavy rain washed away key installations in the town.

"Residents have been using stream water since parts of the waterworks were washed away. Power has been cut off in most parts of the town, and the hospital has lost its medical kit," Mpishi told Reuters.
He said the government had airlifted medical staff and supplies to the area on Wednesday and work to repair water and electricity systems had also started.
"We expect normal water and power supplies to be restored within a few days," Mpishi said.
The rain disrupted production at Zambia's largest coal mine, Maamba Collieries Ltd (MCL), after its open pit was flooded and equipment at its central works was damaged.
Mpishi said there was no indication when the mine would resume normal operations.
"Even if the equipment was replaced the mine could not resume operations for as long as water supplies remained inadequate," he said.
The Zambian Privatisation Agency put the mine up for sale in October last year. It has the capacity to produce 600,000 to 800,000 metric tonnes per year.
